turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Afternoon. I'm Dr Pillay. Have a seat, both of you. What brings you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Shame, Doctor, he won't tell you himself. Since he was retrenched he isn't sleeping, he's got no energy, and he just sits.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): I am fine, Doctor. Truly. My wife wished me to attend, and I did not want to be difficult.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're not being difficult. When you say you are fine, how have the days been going?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): The firm retrenched several of us. They were courteous about it. I have tried to be courteous in return.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): I follow that. I was asking about you, though, the sleep and the energy, not the letter from work.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Forgive me, Doctor. I answered the wrong thing. The sleep has not been good.
[SEG0008] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's in the kitchen at three in the morning. I hear the kettle.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Can you date it for me, Mr Venter? When did this begin?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): I cannot give you a date, Doctor. Last winter, or the winter before. It is not clear in my mind.
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was after the retrenchment, that I know, but the month escapes me as well. Somewhere in the cold months.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the date loose, then. Is it most nights, or only some?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Most nights, I would say. I fall asleep, and then I am awake, and I stay awake.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Roughly how many hours would you—
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, and it's every night with that kettle, I was just—
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's all right. Mr Venter, roughly how many hours of sleep?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Perhaps three, sometimes four. I do not wish to overstate it.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): And through the day, your energy?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): It is low, Doctor. I attend to what is necessary, but there is very little drive.
[SEG0020] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He used to walk early, before the traffic. The shoes just stay by the door now.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy?
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Load shedding was hectic last night, the whole of Rondebosch dark, and I nearly—
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. The cricket, the garden, even the Sunday paper. I begin, and then I set them aside.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your mood. Would you say it is low?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I am not in tears, if that is the question. I am flat. That is the accurate word.
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does get tearful. I saw it on Tuesday, when the old photos came up on his phone.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): I would not call it tearful, Doctor. I was quiet. Nothing more than that.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll hold both versions and not push you to agree. How is your appetite?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): The mealies needed water, so I saw to the garden. They were looking tired.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I meant food, Mr Venter. Are you eating as usual?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. Much as before. I finish what is put on the plate.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any change in your weight, clothes looser or tighter?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): I have not weighed myself. My clothes fit as they did.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about concentration, the paper, a conversation?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): The newspaper is hard going. I lose the thread. A short conversation I can still follow.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am going to ask this gently, and a plain answer is best. Have you had thoughts of harming yourself, or of life not being worth going on with?
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. I have not had those thoughts. I would not do such a thing to my wife.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you. That is clear. Is there hopelessness in it, or mainly this flat, tired feeling?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Not hopeless, Doctor. Flat, and tired. I do still think matters can improve.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain, headaches, anything in the chest?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): No pain, Doctor. My chest is quite all right.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines for this, now or earlier? Even something you only tried.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): The GP prescribed amitriptyline, ten milligrams at night, for sleep. I stopped it in March. It left me dull-headed the following day.
[SEG0044] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There was also a script for sertraline. It's still in the—
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): I never took that, Doctor. I did not collect it from the chemist.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): So sertraline was never started. I won't count it. Anything you take every day now?
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing regular, Doctor. I have been fortunate with my health.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operations over the years?
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): None at all, Doctor.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tobacco, or alcohol?
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. A glass of wine with Sunday lunch, and no more than that.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): At home it's the two of you?
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. A small place in Rondebosch. Our children are grown, and they live in Durban.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): And work, at present?
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): I am not working. I was retrenched from the accounts office. I have submitted a few applications. It moves slowly.
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): In the family, has anyone been treated for low mood?
[SEG0057] person_3 (PATIENT): My late father had depression, and he was treated for it. I would not wish to stretch the comparison.

[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me think aloud for a moment. Broken sleep, little energy, interest fallen away, all after the retrenchment, and you are clear there is no thought of harm. That can be a depressive episode, and it can also be the strain of adjusting to a large loss. I do not want to fix a label today.
[SEG0059] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): But is it serious? Should we be worried, or—
[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): Serious enough to act on, without rushing the name. A tablet such as sertraline is one road. I would rather not start any medicine today.
[SEG0061] person_3 (PATIENT): I would prefer that, Doctor, if you agree. The amitriptyline did not suit me.
[SEG0062] person_1 (DOCTOR): I do agree. If you are no better when we meet again, we can look at a tablet then. It stays an option, not a decision.
[SEG0063] person_3 (PATIENT): That is clear. Thank you, Doctor.
[SEG0064] person_1 (DOCTOR): What I will do is refer you to the counsellor at this clinic. I am sending that through, so they can offer you a proper space to talk.
[SEG0065] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Good. He needs somebody who isn't me going on at him.
[SEG0066] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two practical things from your side. Same bedtime when you can, and leave the phone out of the bed. A short walk most days, even ten minutes, if the energy allows.
[SEG0067] person_3 (PATIENT): I can manage that, Doctor. Walking was my habit.

[SEG0068] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back to me in four weeks, even if the counsellor has not seen you yet. If you are still this flat then, I might send bloods, a thyroid test and a full blood count, so we are not missing something ordinary. Not today.
[SEG0069] person_3 (PATIENT): Four weeks. I shall be here.
[SEG0070] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get him here. And if he slips before then?
[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): Phone the rooms, or come in sooner. If any thought of harm shows up, do not wait for me, go straight to the emergency unit. That is not where things stand today.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

omissions.text: Poor sleep is specifically sleep-maintenance insomnia: he falls asleep, then wakes and stays awake.
Low energy detail: he attends to what is necessary but has very little drive.
Loss of interest examples were given: cricket, gardening, and even the Sunday paper; he starts them and then sets them aside.
Concentration difficulty was qualified: the newspaper is hard going and he loses the thread, but he can still follow a short conversation.
Negative finding not recorded: no pain.
Negative finding not recorded: no chest symptoms/"my chest is quite all right," not just no chest pain.
Medication history missing: sertraline was prescribed previously but never started because he did not collect it from the chemist.
Medication plan detail missing: the doctor specifically preferred not to start any medicine today, and the patient agreed, preferring to avoid medication because amitriptyline did not suit him.
Past medical history detail not recorded: he reports taking nothing regular currently and says he has otherwise been fortunate with his health.
Safety-net detail missing: if he worsens before four weeks, they were advised to phone the rooms or come in sooner.
